newsitem.title: USA: Hsing-Hsing to celebrate 25th anniversary at zoo.
newsitem.headline: Hsing-Hsing to celebrate 25th anniversary at zoo.

text.p: He has outlived his mate, entertained millions and endured the Washington habitat longer than five U.S. presidents, but life has not been a bed of bamboo for the National Zoo's giant panda Hsing-Hsing.

Hsing-Hsing has never produced an heir and now is ill with testicular cancer. He is enduring his fifth breeding season without a female after the death of his mate, Ling-Ling, in 1992. At 26 he is very old for a panda, and he has arthritis.

But the zoo still planned to mark on Wednesday morning the 25th anniversary of Hsing-Hsing's arrival, with speeches for the crowd that routinely gathers around his enclosure. The panda will get one of his favourite treats, a blueberry cake.
"I'm sure he'll come out for it," zoo spokesman Bob Hoage said. Hsing-Hsing has been taking some medication for his arthritis and "it seems to have made a young male out of him again," he said.

Hsing-Hsing and Ling-Ling were given to the United States in 1972 by China following a trip there by then-President Richard Nixon. It is estimated that as many as 75 million people -- about three million a year -- have visited the National Zoo's panda exhibit since that time.
Hsing-Hsing "is one of the oldest pandas known to be alive," Hoage said. Since he has been in at the zoo, Presidents Nixon, Ford, Carter, Reagan and Bush have passed through the White House.
Hsing-Hsing's cancer surgery is scheduled for April 23, and doctors will check to see if the disease has spread to any other tissues. "We are optimistic he'll recover," Hoage said.
